title: Romanian prosecutors indict Andrew Tate for trafficking minors, money laundering – Europe live
text:
A British man – identified by local media as controversial manosphere influencer Andrew Tate – was formally indicted by Romanian authorities on Friday for a number of alleged crimes, including trafficking minors, money laundering, and sexual offences.
His older brother – identified by media as Tristan Tate – was also indicted for alleged complicity and seeking to pervert the course of justice.
A press release issued by DIICOT, Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism, outlines a number of alleged offences including alleged sexual exploitation of a minor who was moved to Luton, UK, for the purposes of online pornography.
The press release also includes allegations of attempts to pervert the course of justice by seeking to stop another victim from reporting it to the police.
The two men are not named in the press release, but the authorities said it was part of an investigation into two British citizens, aged 38 and 39 and members of the same family. National news agency Agerpress, Antena3 and Digi24 all identified them as the Tate brothers.
As part of the investigation, the prosecutors also requested that four of their luxury cars – worth €825,000 – are confiscated as part of the probe.
The Tate brothers also face separate proceedings in the US and in the UK.
in Rome
Giorgia Meloni is celebrating her government becoming the longest-serving since the history of the Italian Republic, although she cautioned that “stability is not a record to flaunt”.
Meloni, leader of the far-right Brother of Italy, and her coalition allies will mark the milestone with a festival-style rally in the southern Italian city of Bari on Friday. About 10,000 people will be bussed in from across Italy and Meloni will deliver a speech, essentially launching her campaign ahead of general elections next year.
In a message on social media, Meloni said she welcomed the longevity record “with gratitude and a strong sense of responsibility”.
She added:
“Because stability is not a record to flaunt, but a condition that enables a nation to plan, make decisions, keep its commitments and command respect.”
Meloni came to power in October 2022, becoming Italy’s first female prime minister. Her government has so far lasted 1,413 days – beating by a day the late Silvio Berlusconi’s second administration between June 2021 and April 2005.
Her government has been buoyed by a strong parliamentary majority while Meloni has earned respect overseas after jettisoning her previous hardline rhetoric in favour of cultivating a more moderate, pragmatic image. Still, some of her domestic policies, such as restricting LGBTQ+ rights and vigorously expanding law and order regulations, show her old instincts remain.
But she is now being challenged on the far-right by a former army general, Roberto Vannacci, who in the space of a few months has drawn defectors from all three of the main ruling coalition parties, as well a significant portion of their electorate.
Stability is a major achievement, especially in a country like Italy where governments easily collapse, but with internal infighting beneath the surface, Meloni’s passage towards a second mandate is much less guaranteed than it was a few months ago.
A Romanian lawyer for the Tate brothers responded to the latest move by the Romanian prosecutors (10:38).
“We will examine every aspect of (the ‌indictment) with the same level of scrutiny and we will challenge any evidential, procedural or legal deficiencies through the appropriate judicial process,” a Romanian lawyer for the Tates, Eugen Vidineac, said in a statement quoted by Reuters.
“Our clients continue to reject the allegations against them.“
Discussions ⁠on US negotiators going to ⁠Ukraine ⁠are ongoing, ​and the teams ⁠have spoken about 6 September ⁠as a ​possible ‌date, ‌a source ‌familiar with the matter said, as reported by Reuters.
Russian news agency TASS reported ‌earlier that US negotiators Steve Witkoff ​and Jared Kushner would visit ⁠Russia and Ukraine ​on Saturday ​and ​Sunday.
Back to Ukraine and Russia, Air Tanzania is the first airline to suspend flights to Moscow, attributing the decision to “a routine risk assessment of the operating environment along the route.”
In a post on Facebook, the airline said it was “temporarily” suspending flights to Moscow, insisting that “safety considerations always take precedence over commercial ones.”
The move comes after repeated warning from Ukraine that Russian airspace is becoming unsafe for commercial airlines because of increased military activity, with Kyiv formally notifying the International Civil Aviation Organization of its concerns.
A rapid escalation of Ukrainian military capability in the past few months has allowed Ukraine’s forces to strike at targets around Moscow, St Petersburg and other locations deep inside Russia.
Today’s announcement regarding the Tate brothers is the latest in a series of developments in their legal cases in Romania.
Romanian investigative journalist Andrei Popoviciu wrote for the Guardian last year that “how we handle [Tate] will reveal what kind of country we really are.”
“If Romania’s justice system wants to maintain any credibility, it must remain independent – not just from Washington, but from any external or political influence. Judges, prosecutors and lawmakers must take the allegations against the Tates seriously, and the government must be independent, not least for the sake of the Tates’ alleged victims.”
For what it’s worth, the brothers have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

Russia keeps targeting Ukraine’s energy facilities in its latest round of overnight attacks, part of an ongoing attempt to cripple the country’s power grid ahead of winter.
Odesa region governor Oleh Kiper said that one was died and at least five were injured in the attack.
Over the last few days, strikes continued to hit the capital city of Kyiv as Russia seeks to disrupt daily life by adding daytime attacks to regular night-time attacks.
Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last night that he was preparing to hold further talks with US negotiators in the coming weeks, with tentative dates set for their much-anticipated visit to Kyiv.
I will bring you all the updates on this today.
Separately, Germany braces for the Saxony-Anhalt state election on Sunday, which could see the far-right Alternative für Deutschland in power for the first time since the second world war. Over in Italy, Giorgia Meloni celebrates her record as longest-serving government in the country’s post-war history.
It’s Friday, 4 September 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.
